question: You are tasked with selecting exactly 2 out of 5 nodes (node_0, node_1, node_2, node_3, node_4) to host facilities, with the goal of maximizing the minimum distance between any two selected facilities. The decision variables are binary: each node can either be selected (1) or not selected (0), and for every pair of nodes, a binary variable indicates whether both nodes in the pair are selected. The distances between nodes are derived from the LP constraints, where the distance between node_0 and node_1 is 18 units (1,000,018 - 1,000,000), node_0 and node_2 is 36 units (1,000,036 - 1,000,000), node_0 and node_3 is 28 units (1,000,028 - 1,000,000), node_0 and node_4 is 20 units (1,000,020 - 1,000,000), node_1 and node_0 is 25 units (1,000,025 - 1,000,000), node_1 and node_2 is 37 units (1,000,037 - 1,000,000), node_1 and node_3 is 36 units (1,000,036 - 1,000,000), node_1 and node_4 is 17 units (1,000,017 - 1,000,000), node_2 and node_0 is 42 units (1,000,042 - 1,000,000), node_2 and node_1 is 42 units (1,000,042 - 1,000,000), node_2 and node_3 is 23 units (1,000,023 - 1,000,000), node_2 and node_4 is 46 units (1,000,046 - 1,000,000), node_3 and node_0 is 31 units (1,000,031 - 1,000,000), node_3 and node_1 is 36 units (1,000,036 - 1,000,000), node_3 and node_2 is 11 units (1,000,011 - 1,000,000), node_3 and node_4 is 50 units (1,000,050 - 1,000,000), node_4 and node_0 is 10 units (1,000,010 - 1,000,000), node_4 and node_1 is 29 units (1,000,029 - 1,000,000), node_4 and node_2 is 24 units (1,000,024 - 1,000,000), and node_4 and node_3 is 42 units (1,000,042 - 1,000,000). The constraints ensure that exactly 2 nodes are selected, and for each pair of nodes, the minimum distance between any two selected facilities must be at least as large as the distance between those two nodes if both nodes in the pair are selected. If either node in the pair is not selected, the constraint is relaxed using a large constant (1,000,000). Additionally, the selection of a pair of nodes is only valid if both nodes in the pair are selected, enforced by ensuring that if a pair is selected, both nodes in the pair must be selected, and if both nodes in a pair are selected, the pair must be selected. The solution must ensure that the facilities are optimally dispersed across the network.

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "nodes": [0, 1, 2, 3, 4],
    "num_selected": 2,
    "big_m": 1_000_000,
    # directed distance matrix dist[i][j] (units, after subtracting 1,000,000)
    "dist": {
        (0, 1): 18, (0, 2): 36, (0, 3): 28, (0, 4): 20,
        (1, 0): 25, (1, 2): 37, (1, 3): 36, (1, 4): 17,
        (2, 0): 42, (2, 1): 42, (2, 3): 23, (2, 4): 46,
        (3, 0): 31, (3, 1): 36, (3, 2): 11, (3, 4): 50,
        (4, 0): 10, (4, 1): 29, (4, 2): 24, (4, 3): 42,
    },
}

GOLD_ANSWER = None


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    nodes = d["nodes"]
    dist = d["dist"]
    M = d["big_m"]
    k = d["num_selected"]

    # unordered pairs i < j
    pairs = [(i, j) for i in nodes for j in nodes if i < j]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.N = pyo.Set(initialize=nodes)
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=pairs, dimen=2)

    # selection variable
    model.select = pyo.Var(model.N, within=pyo.Binary)

    # pair-selected indicator
    model.pair = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.Binary)

    # minimum pairwise distance among selected facilities
    model.minDist = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # exactly k nodes selected
    def rule_cardinality(m):
        return sum(m.select[i] for i in m.N) == k
    model.cardinality = pyo.Constraint(rule=rule_cardinality)

    # pair <= select[i]
    def rule_pair_le_i(m, i, j):
        return m.pair[i, j] <= m.select[i]
    model.pair_le_i = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=rule_pair_le_i)

    # pair <= select[j]
    def rule_pair_le_j(m, i, j):
        return m.pair[i, j] <= m.select[j]
    model.pair_le_j = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=rule_pair_le_j)

    # pair >= select[i] + select[j] - 1
    def rule_pair_ge(m, i, j):
        return m.pair[i, j] >= m.select[i] + m.select[j] - 1
    model.pair_ge = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=rule_pair_ge)

    # minDist <= dist[i,j] + M*(1 - pair[i,j])
    def rule_min_dist(m, i, j):
        return m.minDist <= dist[(i, j)] + M * (1 - m.pair[i, j])
    model.min_dist = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=rule_min_dist)

    # objective: maximize the minimum pairwise distance
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.minDist, sense=pyo.maximize)

    return model

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    n = d["num_nodes"]
    pair_list = list(d["dist"].keys())

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    model.N = pyo.Set(initialize=list(range(n)))
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=pair_list, dimen=2)

    # x[i] = 1 if node i is selected
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.N, within=pyo.Binary)
    # y[i,j] = 1 if both i and j are selected
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.Binary)
    # z = minimum pairwise distance among selected facilities
    model.z = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # exactly num_selected nodes selected
    def rule_select(m):
        return sum(m.x[i] for i in m.N) == d["num_selected"]
    model.c_select = pyo.Constraint(rule=rule_select)

    # linkage: y[i,j] <= x[i]
    def rule_y_le_xi(m, i, j):
        return m.y[i, j] <= m.x[i]
    model.c_y_le_xi = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=rule_y_le_xi)

    # linkage: y[i,j] <= x[j]
    def rule_y_le_xj(m, i, j):
        return m.y[i, j] <= m.x[j]
    model.c_y_le_xj = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=rule_y_le_xj)

    # linkage: y[i,j] >= x[i] + x[j] - 1
    def rule_y_ge_pair(m, i, j):
        return m.y[i, j] >= m.x[i] + m.x[j] - 1
    model.c_y_ge_pair = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=rule_y_ge_pair)

    # if both selected, z <= distance between them (relaxed by big-M otherwise)
    def rule_min_dist(m, i, j):
        return m.z <= d["dist"][(i, j)] + d["bigM"] * (1 - m.y[i, j])
    model.c_min_dist = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=rule_min_dist)

    # maximize the minimum pairwise distance
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.z, sense=pyo.maximize)

    return model

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Sets
    model.N = pyo.Set(initialize=d["nodes"])
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=d["pairs"], dimen=2)

    # Variables
    # x[i] = 1 if node i hosts a facility
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.N, within=pyo.Binary)

    # y[i,j] = 1 if both nodes i and j are selected
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.Binary)

    # z = minimum distance between any two selected facilities
    model.z = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Objective: maximize the minimum pairwise distance
    def obj_rule(m):
        return m.z
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # Exactly num_select nodes selected: sum_i x[i] == num_select
    def select_count_rule(m):
        return sum(m.x[i] for i in m.N) == d["num_select"]
    model.select_count = pyo.Constraint(rule=select_count_rule)

    # Pair-definition constraints (each pair i<j):
    #   y[i,j] <= x[i]
    def pair_le_i_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.y[i, j] <= m.x[i]
    model.pair_le_i = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=pair_le_i_rule)

    #   y[i,j] <= x[j]
    def pair_le_j_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.y[i, j] <= m.x[j]
    model.pair_le_j = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=pair_le_j_rule)

    #   y[i,j] >= x[i] + x[j] - 1
    def pair_ge_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.y[i, j] >= m.x[i] + m.x[j] - 1
    model.pair_ge = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=pair_ge_rule)

    # Big-M link: z <= dist[i,j] + M*(1 - y[i,j])
    # (if pair selected, z <= dist; if not selected, relaxed)
    def dist_link_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.z <= d["dist"][(i, j)] + d["M"] * (1 - m.y[i, j])
    model.dist_link = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=dist_link_rule)

    return model

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    m.N = pyo.Set(initialize=d["nodes"], ordered=True)
    m.P = pyo.Set(initialize=d["pairs"], dimen=2, ordered=True)

    m.x = pyo.Var(m.N, within=pyo.Binary)
    m.z = pyo.Var(m.P, within=pyo.Binary)
    m.D = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, None))

    def rule_cardinality(mm):
        return sum(mm.x[n] for n in mm.N) == d["K"]

    m.cardinality = pyo.Constraint(rule=rule_cardinality)

    def rule_pair_le_i(mm, i, j):
        return mm.z[i, j] <= mm.x[i]

    m.pair_le_i = pyo.Constraint(m.P, rule=rule_pair_le_i)

    def rule_pair_le_j(mm, i, j):
        return mm.z[i, j] <= mm.x[j]

    m.pair_le_j = pyo.Constraint(m.P, rule=rule_pair_le_j)

    def rule_pair_ge_both(mm, i, j):
        return mm.z[i, j] >= mm.x[i] + mm.x[j] - 1

    m.pair_ge_both = pyo.Constraint(m.P, rule=rule_pair_ge_both)

    def rule_min_distance(mm, i, j):
        return mm.D <= d["dist"][(i, j)] + d["M"] * (1 - mm.z[i, j])

    m.min_distance = pyo.Constraint(m.P, rule=rule_min_distance)

    m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.D, sense=pyo.maximize)
    return m
